questions.question: Which Power BI component is primarily used to build data models and author reports on a Windows PC?
questions.explanation: Power BI Desktop is the free Windows authoring tool for connecting to data, modelling and designing reports, which are then published to the Service.

questions.question: In Power BI, what is Power Query mainly used for?
options: Extracting and transforming data before loading it
questions.explanation: Power Query is the ETL layer (M language) used to connect to sources and shape/clean data before it loads into the model.

questions.question: In a star schema, what does a fact table typically contain?
options: Descriptive attributes such as product names
Only the date hierarchy for the model
Numeric events/transactions with keys to dimensions
Security roles mapped to user emails
questions.explanation: Fact tables store measurable events (sales amounts, quantities) plus foreign keys that relate to descriptive dimension tables.

questions.question: A Product table (one row per ProductID) relates to a Sales table with many rows per ProductID. What is the cardinality from Product to Sales?
questions.explanation: Each product appears once in Product and many times in Sales, so the relationship is one-to-many from Product to Sales.

questions.question: Which DAX expression correctly defines a measure for total sales from a Sales[Amount] column?
questions.explanation: SUM takes a single column; SUMX requires a table and expression, and the other forms are not valid DAX.

questions.question: Which visual is most suitable for showing a single headline KPI value like Total Revenue?
questions.explanation: A Card visual displays a single aggregated value prominently, which is ideal for a headline KPI.

questions.question: After publishing a report to the Power BI Service, where is it stored so colleagues can collaborate on it?
questions.explanation: Published content lives in a Service workspace, where access, sharing and apps are managed.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a slicer on a Power BI report page?
options: To create a new calculated table
To let users filter other visuals interactively
To change the data source credentials
questions.explanation: A slicer is an on-canvas filter control that filters other visuals on the page (and optionally synced pages).

questions.question: What is a key difference between a calculated column and a measure in Power BI?
options: A column is computed at refresh and stored; a measure is computed at query time
A measure is stored in the model at refresh; a column is evaluated per visual
Both are computed at query time but columns ignore filters
Columns can only use M code while measures use DAX
questions.explanation: Calculated columns are evaluated row by row during refresh and stored in the model, while measures are evaluated on demand in the current filter context.

questions.question: What does CALCULATE([Total Sales], Product[Color] = "Red") return in a visual already filtered to Color = Blue (default behaviour)?
options: Blank, because Red and Blue filters intersect
Sales for both Red and Blue products combined
Sales for Blue products only, ignoring the Red filter
Sales for Red products, overriding the Blue filter on Color
questions.explanation: A boolean filter argument in CALCULATE replaces existing filters on that column (it is wrapped in FILTER(ALL(Product[Color]),...)), so Red sales are returned.

questions.question: A calculated column uses SUM(Sales[Amount]) in the Sales table without CALCULATE. What does each row show?
options: The Amount value of the current row only
A blank value because row context is invalid
The grand total of Amount for the whole table
The running total up to the current row
questions.explanation: Row context does not filter tables by itself; without CALCULATE's context transition, SUM sees the whole (unfiltered) table in a calculated column.

questions.question: Which requirement must a date table meet for DAX time intelligence functions like TOTALYTD to work reliably?
options: Only dates that appear in the fact table
A contiguous set of dates covering full years, with no gaps
Dates stored as text in YYYYMMDD format
One row per month instead of per day
questions.explanation: Time intelligence functions need a date table with a unique, contiguous date column spanning complete years; marking it as a date table is recommended.

questions.question: By default, how does a one-to-many relationship propagate filters in Power BI?
options: From the one side to the many side (single direction)
From the many side to the one side only
It does not propagate filters until enabled
questions.explanation: One-to-many relationships default to single cross-filter direction, filtering from the dimension (one) side to the fact (many) side.

questions.question: A source table has columns Jan, Feb, Mar holding monthly sales. Which Power Query step converts it to Month/Value rows?
questions.explanation: Unpivot turns column headers into attribute values with corresponding values in rows, producing a tidy Month/Value layout.

questions.question: How is static row-level security defined in Power BI Desktop?
options: By hiding columns in the Fields pane
By adding page-level filters to each report page
By creating roles with DAX filter expressions on tables
By setting workspace permissions to Viewer
questions.explanation: RLS roles use DAX table filter expressions; users mapped to a role in the Service see only rows that satisfy the filter.

questions.question: An imported dataset uses an on-premises SQL Server. What is required for scheduled refresh in the Power BI Service?
questions.explanation: The Service cannot reach on-premises sources directly; an on-premises data gateway securely bridges the connection for refresh.

questions.question: Why does a measure reference like [Total Sales] inside a calculated column return a different value per row than SUM(Sales[Amount])?
options: Measure references are implicitly wrapped in CALCULATE, causing context transition
Measures always ignore row context and return blanks
Measures are cached per row during refresh
Calculated columns convert measures into iterators like SUMX
questions.explanation: Every measure reference is implicitly wrapped in CALCULATE, which converts the current row context into an equivalent filter context (context transition).

questions.question: Which measure returns sales for all products while keeping any filter on Product[Category]?
questions.explanation: ALLEXCEPT removes all filters from the Product table except those on the listed column, so the Category filter is retained.

questions.question: Why does Microsoft guidance advise caution with bi-directional cross-filtering?
options: It prevents measures from using CALCULATE
It can create ambiguous filter paths and hurt performance
questions.explanation: Bi-directional filtering can introduce ambiguity between multiple paths and extra query cost, so it should be used only where needed.

questions.question: Which DAX function is typically used in a dynamic RLS role filter to match the signed-in user's email/UPN?
questions.explanation: USERPRINCIPALNAME() returns the user's UPN in the Service, which is compared against a user column for dynamic RLS.

questions.question: Which statement about DirectQuery mode compared with Import mode is correct?
options: Queries are sent to the source at view time, so data is current but visuals may be slower
Data is compressed into VertiPaq, so it is always faster than Import
It removes all DAX limitations present in Import mode
It requires scheduled refresh to show any new data
questions.explanation: DirectQuery does not cache data; each interaction queries the source, giving near-real-time data at the cost of performance and some DAX/Power Query limitations.

questions.question: Which expression returns sales for the same period in the previous year, given a marked Date table?
questions.explanation: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR returns the dates shifted back one year and is used as a filter argument inside CALCULATE.
